assumptions: The M1 approved-contract hash is available and binds the worker to its plan.
Treehouse is installed or installable in the canonical WSL2 environment; doctor will report it.
One worktree equals one write track; retries within a valid contract reuse the same worktree.
content.goal: A single Pi worker executes one leased task end to end: MNFS grants a Treehouse worktree lease, the worker records a durable CLAIM in SQLite, and a restarted lead process recovers the claim and lease state without losing or duplicating work.

acceptanceCriteria: `mnfs lease grant --mission MIS-002 --json` creates a worktree outside the checkout and persists the lease row plus LEASE_GRANTED event atomically.
Granting a second lease for the same task fails with a typed conflict error.
`mnfs lease release` removes the worktree and persists LEASE_RELEASED; release is idempotent.
features.outcome: MNFS can allocate, inspect and release exactly one worktree lease through a narrow process adapter.
features.title: Treehouse lease adapter

acceptanceCriteria: CLAIM insert and CLAIM_OPENED event commit in one transaction bound to the lease and contract hash.
Worker completion records completed-by-worker without transitioning the task to accepted.
Invalid transitions (e.g. accept before claim) fail with typed errors and leave state unchanged.
features.outcome: A worker claim is a durable SQLite state machine, not an in-memory message.
features.title: Durable CLAIM lifecycle

milestones.outcome: SQLite is the single source of truth for one lease and one claim, recoverable across process restarts.
milestones.title: Durable claim and lease core

acceptanceCriteria: Worker starts with cwd set to the leased worktree and receives the contract hash and the fixed MNFS-defined demo task.
The fixed demo task is a trivial, deterministic repository edit defined by MNFS that proves the loop end to end.
Worker completion is reported as a notification; durable state changes only through MNFS commands.
Worker failure or crash leaves the claim open and the lease intact for reuse or release.
features.outcome: One Pi worker session executes the task inside its leased worktree, bound to the mission contract.
features.title: Pi worker launch in leased worktree

acceptanceCriteria: `mnfs recover --json` from a new process lists the open claim, its lease and the actual worktree, flagging any divergence.
Recovery reads only SQLite and the filesystem; no transcript, log-scraping or terminal-output parsing participates in state reconstruction.
Recovery after a simulated lead crash produces the same state as before the crash with no duplicate claim.
`mnfs claim accept` validates gate criteria, records CLAIM_ACCEPTED, and is the only path to acceptance.
features.outcome: A fresh lead process reconstructs claim and lease state and only an MNFS gate accepts completion.
features.title: Lead restart recovery and gate acceptance

milestones.outcome: A real Pi worker runs in the leased worktree and the lead survives a restart with full state recovery.
milestones.title: One-worker execution and recovery

questions.answer: MNFS defines a fixed demo task: a trivial deterministic repository edit that proves the full lease/claim/recovery loop.
questions.question: What is the concrete task the single worker executes in this slice (e.g. a trivial repository edit proving the loop) — should MNFS define a fixed demo task or accept an operator-supplied task description?

questions.answer: Herdr arrives later as a separate mission, not as a milestone of MIS-002.
questions.question: Herdr is optional and outside every deciding criterion of this slice; should it later arrive as a separate mission or as a follow-up milestone after this slice is accepted?

risks.description: Treehouse behavior in WSL2 diverges from expectations (paths, permissions, cleanup), breaking lease release or recovery.
risks.mitigation: Wrap Treehouse behind a narrow adapter with a fake for tests; run real acceptance in the canonical WSL2 environment before closing the slice.

risks.description: Crash between worktree creation and SQLite commit leaves an orphaned worktree or a lease row without a worktree.
risks.mitigation: Order operations so SQLite intent is written first; recovery command detects and repairs divergence idempotently, with tests for both orphan directions.

risks.description: Worker completion messages get treated as durable completion, violating the gate rule.
risks.mitigation: Model acceptance as an explicit MNFS gate command with tests proving a worker message alone never changes accepted state.

excluded: Herdr integration: explicitly optional, never part of any deciding acceptance criterion, and deferred out of this slice.
Multiple concurrent workers, worker pools or scheduling policies.
Automatic merge or integration of worker output into main.
Review UI changes in Lavish beyond what M1 already provides.
Port, database or container isolation policies beyond worktree isolation.
included: Treehouse lease adapter limited to allocate, inspect and release of one worktree write track per ADR-0003.
Durable CLAIM lifecycle in SQLite: claimed, completed-by-worker, accepted-by-gate, released.
Single Pi worker launch bound to the leased worktree and the mission contract hash.
Lead restart recovery command that reconciles SQLite claim/lease state against actual worktrees.
CLI surfaces with --json output for lease, claim, recovery and gate acceptance.

successCriteria: Deciding M2 proof: one Pi worker uses a leased Treehouse worktree, writes a durable CLAIM, and a restarted lead recovers it — with no transcript or terminal parsing anywhere in the recovery path.
One task can be dispatched to exactly one Pi worker under a Treehouse worktree lease created and released through MNFS.
The worker CLAIM is persisted durably in SQLite with a matching append-only event before any work product is accepted.
Killing and restarting the lead process recovers the open CLAIM and lease from SQLite alone, with no orphaned worktree and no duplicate claim.
No deciding acceptance criterion depends on Herdr; the slice is provable with Herdr entirely absent.
Only an MNFS gate marks the claim accepted; a worker completion message alone never transitions the task to done.
The full flow is operable through strict human/JSON CLI contracts and passes verification in the canonical WSL2 environment.
content.title: M2 smallest one-worker vertical slice
